gloss_distractors: shared with only a few people
senses.definition: In the most prominent position, where nobody can miss it.
senses.caution: Whatever you put there also gets the most questions, and a person put there answers for it. It is spoken American English and sounds casual in a formal paper.
senses.example: Put the cost of doing nothing front and center. Everything else can go in the appendix.

cues.text: You are advising a colleague on a board deck, and the risk they buried on slide fourteen is the one thing the board most needs to see.
A sponsor asks what actually changed in the new strategy, and the honest answer is that a topic which used to sit in the appendix is now the first thing anybody sees.
You are hanging pictures and want one particular photograph in the most visible spot in the room rather than tucked off to the side.
A friend asks what you are prioritising now that the children have left home, and the answer is something you used to squeeze in around everything else.

distractors: Done quietly so as not to be seen doing it.
Lasting only briefly, and meant to.
Present in scattered, isolated places rather than across the whole.
Understood by only a small group, because it assumes background most people lack.
Big enough to matter, said of an amount or a change.
